title: Foundation MCP dispatch host
description: Objective: land the missing real daemon process/transport consumer so Foundation self-hosting does not inject a fake StdioDispatchPort/HttpDispatchPort in its E2E harness. Deliverable: a bounded daemon host executable that opens the project store, composes authenticated @moe/mcp stdio and Streamable HTTP dispatch ports with the published @moe/daemon Foundation ingress surface, routes coordination/session traffic, supports graceful drain/restart, and emits readiness/shutdown receipts used by J3. NOT in scope: custom WebSocket MCP, control-room UI, multi-node activation, release publication, or canary assertions. Depends on Foundation daemon ingress surface. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/host/foundation-host.ts/.js, foundation-host.test.ts, and apps/daemon/package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml only for @moe/mcp; add a bin/script only if needed for the executable. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck plus a plain-Node stdio smoke.
definitionOfDone: The executable composes real @moe/mcp dispatch with @moe/daemon/store/session/coordination surfaces; no injected test dispatcher or deep import decides auth, command, or durable outcomes.

Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP requests reach the same bounded authenticated command path; malformed/oversized/forged/stale input asserts exact transport and daemon reason codes/layers and commits nothing.

The host publishes deterministic readiness, process identity, project/store identity, and graceful-shutdown receipts; restart reopens the same durable state and drives production reconciliation before accepting commands.
Concurrent duplicate command delivery leaves one durable decision and one authority holder; advisory session/terminal text never invokes command authority.
Plain-Node stdio smoke plus MCP/daemon/repo gates exit 0; only explicit owned paths and the exact @moe/mcp manifest addition are committed.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
Only official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP are permitted; do not add a custom MCP-over-WebSocket protocol.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the registry gap, which is the whole of DoD 1 and DoD 2's Foundation reach. So `foundation.dispatch` (work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:39) and `foundation.verification` (evidence/foundation-verification-contracts.ts:24) are unreachable from EVERY transport — stdio, Streamable HTTP and the HTTP listener alike — because all three funnel through `handleCommandRequest` and the registry decides what it admits. Note the vocabulary was extracted into `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` (123 lines) very recently by a peer, so re-confirm the file layout before editing. In `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` write RED cases: each Foundation kind is admitted, carries its own schema version, requires its declared payload keys, and refuses a foreign or malformed payload with the exact stable code and refusing layer. Pin the wired-kind roster BY HAND so an added kind must be transcribed rather than silently absorbed.

Wire the two Foundation families into the vocabulary and registry. In `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` add both kinds the way the existing constant-keyed kinds are added — `CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KIND`, `EFFECT_ACTIVATE_COMMAND_KIND`, `JOURNAL_APPEND_COMMAND_KIND` and `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_COMMAND_KIND` are the template at :1-9, :57-58, :64-71 and :90-91: import the kind and its payload-key tuple from the owning contracts module, widen `WiredCommandKind`, give each its capability set, and add its `PAYLOAD_KEYS` entry. Use `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_KEYS` and `FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_REQUEST_KEYS`, which the Foundation surface already publishes — do NOT retype either tuple. In `daemon-command-registry.ts` extend the `schemaVersion` ladder at :121-130 with `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_SCHEMA_VERSION` and route each kind to its service. DECIDE CAPABILITY DELIBERATELY: both commands activate real execution authority, so they belong with WORK at minimum — and if either must be operator-only, add it to `OPERATEUR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`'s set rather than leaving the choice implicit. Keep the vocabulary file under 250 lines (123 today) and the registry under 250 (226 today — tight, so budget this edit).

TDD the receipts, which are DoD 3 and do not exist anywhere: `grep -rn "readinessReceipt|ReadinessRecord|shutdownReceipt|ReadyReceipt" apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO. Today readiness is only a log line (`daemon-entry.ts:227`, `options.log?.(\`listening on ${started.origin}\`)`). Write `apps/daemon/src/host/foundation-receipts.test.ts` RED for a receipts module carrying process identity, project identity, store identity, and the readiness / graceful-shutdown pair. DETERMINISTIC MEANS NO CLOCK, and that is the load-bearing constraint: assert that two receipt builds over identical inputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and that the module reads neither `Date.now()` nor `new Date()` — any instant must arrive as a validated input, exactly as `importCommittedAt` and the effect reducer already do elsewhere in this repo. Cover the refusal arms with exact code and layer: absent store identity, absent project identity, and a shutdown receipt requested before readiness was ever published. Assert the shutdown receipt is idempotent BY REFUSAL rather than silently, matching the `DAEMON_ENTRY_ALREADY_STOPPED` discipline at daemon-entry.ts:189-190.

Implement `apps/daemon/src/host/foundation-receipts.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge — every sibling directory in apps/daemon/src ships git-tracked bridges, and without one the module is invisible at runtime while tsc and vitest both stay green. This is a NEW directory, so the bridge is easy to forget. Exports: the frozen receipt schema version, a frozen refusal code list with its own layer constant, and pure builders for the readiness and shutdown receipts. PURE BY CONSTRUCTION: no clock, no filesystem, no store handle — identities and any instant arrive as validated inputs, which is what makes DoD 3's "deterministic" a property of the type rather than a promise in a comment. Target <=250 physical lines; this module should land well under that.

Emit the receipts from the two PROCESS entries, not from the composition. `daemon-entry.ts` is at 244 lines against a 250 target — one edit crosses it — so leave it alone and wire the entries instead: `daemon-main.ts` (99 lines) already owns the lifecycle, calling `options.onStarted?.(started.shutdown)` at :82 and registering SIGINT/SIGTERM at :89-96, so publish readiness where it currently logs and the shutdown receipt on the signal path. `mcp-main.ts` (58 lines) has NO signal handling at all — grep for SIGTERM/SIGINT/shutdown returns nothing — so it needs the graceful-drain half added alongside its receipt. DO NOT add a third entrypoint and do not reimplement either transport; rail 4 and the reopen reason both forbid it, and `createStdioMcpServer` and `createHttpMcpAdapter` are already composed here. Note `daemon-entry.ts:202` documents that reconciliation runs BEFORE the listener — that half of DoD 3 is already satisfied for the HTTP daemon; assert it rather than rebuilding it, and check whether the stdio entry shares that ordering.

Prove DoD 2 and DoD 4 at the seam, not at the unit. Both transports reach the same bounded authenticated path through `createMcpDispatchPort` -> `handleCommandRequest` (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:62-71), so a Foundation command must produce the SAME durable outcome whichever transport carried it. Add tests that drive one Foundation command through the stdio dispatch port and once through the HTTP path and assert the durable decisions are byte-identical. Then DoD 4's two clauses: (a) CONCURRENT DUPLICATE DELIVERY of the same command id leaves exactly ONE durable decision and one authority holder — count the rows out of the store, since "the second call did not throw" is also what a double write looks like; (b) advisory session/terminal text never invokes command authority — drive an advisory query through `dispatchQueryBytes` and assert zero durable decisions were written. Malformed, oversized, forged and stale input each assert the exact transport and daemon codes AND which layer refused, and commit nothing.

Verification gate. The manifest half of DoD 5 is ALREADY SATISFIED and must not be re-done: `apps/daemon/package.json` already declares `@moe/mcp` (verified at plan time), so there is no manifest addition and no `pnpm install` in this task — confirm that before touching either file, and if the dependency really is present, drop package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml from the commit entirely. Run five legs with exit codes captured SEPARATELY: `pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. All resolve by package name (`@moe/mcp` is packages/mcp, `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, both with typecheck and test scripts). READ THE OUTPUT: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 for an absent package, so record the nonzero `Test Files N passed` count for both test legs. Then the PLAIN-NODE STDIO SMOKE DoD 5 names: start `mcp-main.ts` with a real credential and store path, exchange one official MCP stdio request, and confirm the readiness receipt. Run that from PowerShell, not the Bash tool — a prior plain-Node smoke on this repo failed only because Git Bash rewrote paths. `pnpm typecheck` is repo-wide: attribute red by the merge-base-versus-HEAD failing-path delta intersected with owned paths, and disclose foreign red verbatim.

Mutation drills and adversarial review, then stop. THREE drills, each restored before the next, each naming the test that reddens: (i) remove `foundation.verification` from the wired vocabulary — the step-2 admission test must redden, proving the registry entry is what grants reach rather than some incidental passthrough; (ii) make the readiness receipt read `Date.now()` — the byte-identity assertion from step 4 must redden, which is what proves "deterministic" is tested rather than asserted; (iii) make the duplicate-delivery path write a second decision — the row COUNT assertion from step 7 must redden while a return-value-only assertion would still pass, which is exactly why that test counts rows. A drill that reddens the WRONG test, or hangs, is not a pass. Drills run in a SHARED worktree and this vocabulary file is being actively edited by a peer: snapshot each file's hash and restore by CONTENT, never `git checkout`, and re-read the file before restoring in case it moved underneath you. Then run `adversarial-self-review`: two concurrent shutdowns, a readiness receipt requested twice, a Foundation command arriving before reconciliation completes, and per-file line counts — daemon-command-registry.ts must still be under 250 (226 today) and daemon-entry.ts untouched at 244.

⚠️ VERIFIED PRODUCTION DEFECT IN THIS TASK'S SUBJECT AREA — from Yaron's 2026-08-14 product audit, #general 23:06:38Z. **The human explicitly flagged it as "relevant to the blocked Foundation MCP dispatch host task"** — that is this task. Task stays BLOCKED; this is here so the architect who eventually plans it starts from the real state.

**MCP `events.read` serves a permanently frozen page.** `apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts:98` calls `readSubscriptionPage` with no `foldOnce`, and `mcp-main` never seats a baseline or registers a reader. So the endpoint answers, returns a well-formed page, and that page never advances. Severity MEDIUM in the audit, but note the failure mode: **it does not error.** A consumer polling `events.read` gets successful responses forever and simply never sees new events. Nothing fails closed; there is no reason code to observe.

**What this changes for planning:** a dispatch-host DoD that asserts `events.read` returns a valid page would pass today against a frozen one. The property to pin is *advancement* — read, commit new events, read again, and assert the cursor moved and the new events are present. A shape assertion on a single response cannot distinguish a working reader from this bug. That is the same class as the board's rail on assertions quietly detaching from their subject.

- `apps/daemon/src/foundation/` — the entire directory is absent on disk, not just `foundation-surface.{ts,js}`. The original block premise holds.

Do not promote this task on the audit finding — the finding sharpens the eventual DoD, it does not clear the dependency. Two of this task's own prerequisites are still blocked behind the durable Claude attempt-dispatch chain.

**One more from the same audit, in the hardening backlog and squarely in this task's territory:** the MCP HTTP session registry grows unbounded, and `close()` never releases daemon-side bindings. Whoever plans the dispatch host should treat session lifetime as in-scope rather than assuming the existing transport manages it.

BLOCK EVIDENCE (step-2). The approved plan's core — wiring `foundation.dispatch` / `foundation.verification` into `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` + `daemon-command-registry.ts` — is IMPOSSIBLE within this task's owned paths. Four independent blockers, each measured at HEAD 8222b9e.

1. CLOSED ENUM, IN A PACKAGE THIS TASK DOES NOT OWN.
`CommandRegistryEntry.kind` is typed `RuntimeCommandKind` and `CommandRegistry = ReadonlyMap<RuntimeCommandKind, CommandRegistryEntry>` (apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts:176,181). `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` is `Object.freeze`d with 92 members at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-108, and ZERO begin with `foundation`. Compiled probe, written and deleted in the same command:
```
src/__blocker-probe.ts(5,14): error TS2322: Type '"foundation.dispatch"' is not assignable to type '"approval.decide" | ... 84 more ... | "work.resume"'.
src/__blocker-probe.ts(6,14): error TS2322: Type '"foundation.verification"' is not assignable to type '"approval.decide" | ... 84 more ... | "work.resume"'.
```
So adding either kind to `PAYLOAD_KEYS`/`WiredCommandKind` reddens `entryOf`'s return in the registry. The fix lives in `packages/contracts`, not `apps/daemon`.

2. THE ENVELOPE REFUSES THE KIND BEFORE THE REGISTRY IS EVER CONSULTED.
packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-envelope.ts:141:
`if (!isCommandKind(record["commandKind"])) return commandFailure(invalidInput());`
stdio, Streamable HTTP and the HTTP listener all funnel through `decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes`, so no registry entry is reachable for an unlisted kind. The plan's premise that "one registry edit fixes all three transports" holds only for kinds already in the runtime vocabulary.

3. SYNCHRONOUS HANDLER vs ASYNCHRONOUS SERVICE.
`export type CommandHandler = (input: CommandHandlerInput) => DurableDecision;` (http-contract.ts:167). Both Foundation services are async:
- `createFoundationAttemptService(deps).dispatch(input): Promise<FoundationAttemptOutcome>` (work/foundation-attempt-service.ts:106)
- `createFoundationVerificationService(deps).verify(input): Promise<FoundationVerificationOutcome>` (evidence/foundation-verification-service.ts:54)
A sync handler cannot return either decision.

4. BINARY REQUEST FIELD vs JsonObject PAYLOAD.
`FoundationAttemptDispatchRequest.activationRequestBytes` is a `Uint8Array`, enforced structurally at work/foundation-attempt-codec.ts:89:
`if (!(bytes instanceof Uint8Array) || bytes.byteLength === 0 || bytes.byteLength > MAX_BYTES) return refuseLocal("FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_MALFORMED");`
`RuntimeCommandEnvelope.payload` is a `JsonObject` and the registry's `requestOf` JSON-encodes it. A base64 string dies on that exact guard.

BLOCKERS 3 AND 4 SURVIVE CLOSING THE ENUM. So the obvious workaround — re-mapping Foundation onto an existing runtime kind such as `effect.activate` or `evidence.run` — does not rescue it either.

BONUS GAP: `FoundationAttemptDeps.captureResult` has ZERO production producers repo-wide. `grep -rn "captureResult" apps/ packages/ --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.ts'` returns only the interface declaration (foundation-attempt-service.ts:42) and the service's own call site (:144). Every caller today is a test — so a registry entry, even if reachable, would have no production dependency to compose.
